question: What kind of joining is described for the powers of will and the rest?
premises: The powers beginning with will can be joined together.
This joining is described as consisting of agitation.
It applies both to same-kind powers and to those marked by agitation and nonagitation.
inference: Thus the joining of these powers is fundamentally an agitation.
uncertainties: The scope of kṣobhākṣobhātmanām is slightly ambiguous; it may refer to powers or to states.
plain_english: The joining of the same-kind powers, beginning with will, is said to be a form of agitation, and this also applies to those whose nature involves both agitation and nonagitation.
